title: Paper model manifest
description: The models Paper will resolve, verify and activate. Lemonade's own server_models.json carries recipe, checkpoint and size and NO license and NO per-model digest — checked against 11.7.0's shipped resources/server_models.json, where `kokoro-v1` is a checkpoint, a recipe and a rounded gigabyte count and nothing else. So it cannot be the provenance record, and this is. A gallery entry is untrusted input until it has resolved to an entry here. Meaning of each field: dev-docs/plans/phase-15-the-companion.md, WI-15.1; the enforcement is src-tauri/crates/tauri-plugin-inference/src/manifest.rs.

$schema.description: Relative path of this schema, so editors validate the file in place.

version.description: The manifest format. A file declaring a version this build does not speak is REFUSED, never read as version 1 — a future format silently reinterpreted is a catalogue scrambled with every field looking fine.

models.description: One entry per model Paper offers. Order is display order.

id.description: Stable identifier, and also a directory name under models/ — hence the closed alphabet. Unique across the manifest.

label.description: What the settings pane calls it. Written for a reader, not derived from the checkpoint name.

modality.description: What the model does. `text` binds the companion and the gloss; `speech` binds Test voice. The set is closed because each modality is a code path, not a label.

license.description: SPDX identifier where one exists, else the license's published name. Recorded because Lemonade's catalogue does not carry it and Paper resolves the artifact rather than redistributing it — the reader is entitled to know the terms before a multi-gigabyte download.

backend.description: Which runtime backend loads it. Closed, because an unrecognised backend is not something to pass through to the daemon and hope.

artifacts.description: The files this model is made of. AN ARRAY, not a single file, because one model is routinely more than one artifact: Kokoro is a graph plus a voice pack, and a large GGUF is published as numbered shards. A schema with one `file` field would have forced a fake second model entry to carry a voice file that is not a model.

file.description: The artifact's file name inside models/<id>/. A name, not a path — there is nothing here to traverse with.

source.description: Where the artifact is fetched from. HTTPS only: these are the only URLs in the system that are not loopback, and each is a manifest constant rather than anything a caller supplies.

sha256.description: The artifact's SHA-256. Checked before activation; a mismatch refuses the model and leaves the previous slot live.

bytes.description: The artifact's exact byte count. Checked BEFORE the digest, because a truncated download is the common failure and a stat is cheaper than hashing gigabytes.

role.description: What this artifact is to the model. `weights` is the file the backend loads; `voices` is Kokoro's voice pack. Closed, so a new kind of artifact is a deliberate change rather than a string nobody validates.

parameters.description: Human-readable parameter count, for the settings row. Display only.

quantization.description: Quantization label, for the settings row. Display only.

note.description: Why this model is here, for a maintainer reading the manifest rather than the plan.
